name: Relfydess

lead: Relfydess is a liquid botulinum toxin type A from Galderma that smooths frown lines between the brows, leaving a fresher-looking upper face once the injection takes effect. Its draw is that it comes ready to use rather than needing to be mixed.

Like other type A toxins, it weakens the injected muscles by blocking nerve signals, so the lines above them soften. Its Phase 3 READY-1 trial randomized adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines 3 to 1 to the toxin or placebo over six months and reported patient-assessed effectiveness and satisfaction. Off-label uses appear in case reports, such as a 2026 report on Frey's syndrome.

paras: A clinician injects the frown-line area in an office visit, and the toxin's effect fades over months, so people repeat treatments to maintain the look. It is used as part of the same upper-face routine as other toxins.

It is a prescription injectable, and like other botulinum toxins its effect is temporary and carries class warnings about spread of toxin effect. Independent literature is still limited, and off-label uses are documented only in case reports.

angle.text: Relfydess is a ready-to-use liquid toxin that people choose to smooth frown lines, with the visible softening appearing once the injection takes effect. It relaxes the frown muscles so glabellar lines ease and the upper face looks fresher. Its frown-line use is backed by a Phase 3 trial.

lead: Relfydess (relabotulinumtoxinA) is a ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin type A made by Galderma, developed with a technology the company calls PEARL to produce a complex-free formulation.[1] Unlike freeze-dried toxins, it does not require reconstitution.[1]

Its Phase 3 READY-1 trial enrolled adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines, randomized 3 to 1 to relabotulinumtoxinA or placebo over six months, and reported patient-assessed effectiveness and satisfaction.[1] A published 2026 case report describes off-label use for Frey's syndrome.[2]

paras: The product is presented as a liquid toxin that is ready to inject, made through PEARL technology, which the authors of the READY-1 report describe as yielding a highly effective, complex-free formulation.[1]

In READY-1, adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines were randomized 3:1 to relabotulinumtoxinA or placebo in a six-month study. A 2025 paper in Aesthetic Surgery Journal reported the patient-assessed outcomes for line improvement and satisfaction.[1] A 2026 case report described a 72-year-old man treated off-label with intradermal injections for gustatory sweating after parotidectomy.[2]
Adverse-event findings from the trials were not reviewed for this entry. Botulinum toxins as a class are prescription-only.[1]
